Print-ready materials

Detective Checklist

Keep this open while you investigate

Start with your SIFT moves

  • Stop: don’t share or believe it yet. How does it make you feel?
  • Investigate the source: who made this? Can you trust them?
  • Find it somewhere else: does another trustworthy place tell the same story?
  • Trace it back: find the original photo, book, or story

If it’s a picture, look for these:

  • Zoom in close: melted hands, smudged faces, scrambled letters
  • Check the light: do the shadows make sense?
  • Ask where it came from: a real person, place, and camera?

If it’s writing, look for these:

  • Real names: “experts say” with no names is a ghost source
  • Use what you know: does it even make sense?
  • Check another place: does a trusted site tell the same story?
A Classroom Media Detective Game

Authentic or AI?

Ten mystery cards: amazing pictures, news stories, and posts. Some are completely real. Some were made by AI. First we solve four teaching cards together and learn the SIFT moves. Then your class must decide, share the clues, and check the source, because a detective never just guesses!

1 · ExamineLook closely and talk it out
2 · Think & WriteClaim, clues, and a SIFT check
3 · Vote & RevealFind out the truth together
Teacher's Quick Guide · how to run this in class (1-minute read)

What this is: a slideshow you drive from the front of the room. Nothing advances on its own, and hidden clues stay hidden until you reveal them, so you set the pace and the discussion.

The flow: Detective Training (6 short slides, ≈10 min) teaches the SIFT moves and 3 clues for pictures + 3 clues for writing. Then come 10 case cards. Cards 1-4 are teaching cards you solve together: an AI picture, then a real picture; an AI article, then a real article. Each one spotlights one SIFT move (S, T, I, F). Cards 5-10 are the game. Every card runs Examine → Think & Write → Vote & Reveal: the last screen opens on the class vote (hands up!), then one press of → shows the truth.

Pacing ideas: one class period = training + the 4 teaching cards; the game cards another day. Or make it a routine: one card a day. Completed cards are saved on this device, and next time you open the game a Continue button jumps straight to where you left off. Press Start Over for a fresh class.

The writing activity: each card has a matching half-sheet Case Card students write on, alone or in groups: claim, clues in complete sentences, and the SIFT move they'd use. Print them under Print Materials (top right) and cut each page in two.

Younger students: skip the writing and just talk it out as a class, vote with thumbs up (real) or thumbs sideways (AI), and let volunteers point at clues on the board.

Before class: print the Student Case Cards (scaffolded or open), plus the Teacher Answer Key for yourself.

Driving it: press → (or a presentation clicker) to reveal each hidden clue, then advance. ← steps back. C opens the Detective Checklist. Hovering any image magnifies it for the class. Starting the 2-minute timer takes the card full screen while the class works; → ends it and moves to the vote (Esc just goes back).

Keyboard: → reveal & advance · ← back · C checklist

Exit Ticket

Which detective clue will you use in real life? On the back of your Case Card, draw or write about one thing you saw online that you want to double-check, then tell which SIFT move you would use on it.
